title: President Bidya Devi Bhandari addresses the 106th International Labour Conference
description: President Bidya Devi Bhandari of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal addresses the ILO’s World of Work Summit in Geneva, Switzerland, during it's 106th International Labour Conference.  Find out more about the World of Work Summit: A better future for women at work: http://www.ilo.org/ilc/ILCSessions/106/plenary/world-of-work-summit/lang--en/index.htm   Find out more about the 106th International Labour Conference: http://www.ilo.org/ilc   Find out more about the ILO's activities in Nepal: http://ilo.org/kathmandu/lang--en/index.htm

Thank you. Thank you. Okay. Thank you so much. Thank you. Can I just say a few words about the panel session this morning? There were many issues raised and the recognition of the distance that we still have to travel to get to full equality at work. But one issue that was highlighted, I believe, was the issue of leadership. Leadership politically, leadership in employers organisations, in the trade union movement, in government Your career displays long-term commitment to the values and principles that are very much those of the International Labour Organization. Yours has been a lifelong dedication to achieving a better life for people who we sometimes I think mistakenly describe as ordinary people. I would say all people. Since your student years you have been active in actions to achieve a fairer society. as Minister for the Family and Social Solidarity. The second of our guests is the President of Mauritius, Madam Amina Gurib Fakim. Welcome, Madam President, to our conference. I think it is true to say that the role of the presidency in your country was not perhaps one that you sought, but which you are intent to use to promote social and economic progress in your country. You have been described, I think you have described yourself as a biodiversity scientist, a chemist, a leading expert on the flora of Mauritius, an academic or simply a gardener and And we should not forget to add entrepreneur to the list of your qualities. Your work has brought you international recognition and we are very pleased to add to that today. Since assuming office as President of your country in 2015, you have put your rich experience at the service of your country and your region. And, importantly, given today's theme, for developing an African scientific capacity, playing a key role in launching the alliance for accelerating excellence in science in Africa. You also bring your scientific background to the challenge of climate change, which has been much discussed from this podium in the last two weeks, as an advocate for developing the knowledge that is needed toidya Devi Bhandari. Madam President, you are also extremely welcome here. I'm tempted to say welcome home because you have been a lifelong activist for labour rights, and particularly the rights of women at work. The fight for gender equality has been woven into your lifelong dedication to values and principles. As a charismatic student leader, you stood up for equal rights and opportunity for young people across your country. But you were also part of a broader movement demonstrating great courage during a 15-year struggle 2009 you took on the role of Minister of Defence. Madam Minister, you are very, very welcome here. We are honoured to have you amongst us. Colleagues, we are honoured by the Presidents of all of our guests. You have welcomed them most warmly. I'm tempted to say that this is a three-star event, but it's actually a six-star event. A unique moment when we welcome three women leaders, three presidents of our member states in a setting which could not be more appropriate, the International Labour Conference with the subject, the future of women at work. I thank you all. In the coming year, the International Labour Organization to all the principles of the labour law. annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents an institutional conference address about women leaders, labor rights, gender equality, and the future of women at work. The formal podium speeches and conference setting are consistent with that purpose, with no described payment, credential, investment, prize, or data request.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central content is a public conference event about women's leadership, labour rights and equality at work.
